title: Knee Surgery Rules Sinner Out of the Australian Open
summary:
Jannik Sinner will not play at the Australian Open in January. The 25-year-old Italian tennis star has had surgery on his knee. Tennis Australia has confirmed he will miss the tournament in Melbourne. Sinner said in a social media post on Tuesday that he had an operation on his iliotibial band, a thick band of tissue along the outside of the knee.

Sinner won the Australian Open in both 2024 and 2025. He has not played since winning Wimbledon on 12 July. The main draw of the 2027 Australian Open starts on 17 January. In 2026, Novak Djokovic beat him in a five-set semi-final.

Sinner was the best player of the first half of the season. He won 44 of his singles matches and lost just three. He won five Masters 1000 titles in a row. He then won Wimbledon, beating Djokovic in the semi-finals and Zverev in the final. He ended his season in October. Now his focus is on getting healthy. Andrew Abdo said Sinner loves playing in Melbourne and looks forward to returning for AO 2028.
why_it_matters: Even the best players get hurt, and taking time to heal is part of staying great at sport.
